title: Tech news today, 15 November 2026

items.headline: FAA ground stop: officials cite aging telecom equipment, not AI; investigation ongoing
items.summary: The FAA stopped departures nationwide on 13 November after communication issues hit multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers; AVweb reports the stop ran from about 3:54 p.m. to 8:15 p.m. EST. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed overloaded legacy switches and routers during a contractor's copper-to-fiber work, and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said there was "zero evidence of anything AI-related" (NPR, TechCrunch). This is the official preliminary explanation; the root cause analysis is ongoing.

items.headline: SpaceX catches the Starship upper stage with its launch tower for the first time
items.summary: Reported by CNBC: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket with the launch tower's mechanical arms at Starbase, Texas, on Saturday, 14 November, during Test Flight 15. The ship flew around the Earth 14 times before the catch; it was the first flight on which SpaceX tried to catch both the booster and the upper stage. The Super Heavy booster was not caught: it was diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday and exploded before hitting the water, CNBC reported.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO range implies a valuation of about $1.3 trillion, below earlier talk
items.summary: Reported by Fortune: Anthropic expects to price its shares at $70 to $78 each on 18 November and begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT the following day. Fortune reports that the range translates to a valuation of roughly $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion, lower than the roughly $2 trillion some investors and analysts had projected. This is a summary of news reports, not investment advice.

items.headline: Tesla opens invite-only Cybercab orders for personal use, with a required $299 monthly subscription
items.summary: Reported by Electrek: Tesla's Robotaxi account announced invitations on 13 November; the order page lists the Cybercab at $29,990 before taxes, with a $1,000 non-refundable deposit and estimated delivery in December 2026 in Austin, Texas. A $299-a-month subscription is required to operate the car, which has no steering wheel or pedals, and it works only inside Tesla's Robotaxi service areas, Electrek and Engadget report. Electrek lists Robotaxi service in eight cities: Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth and San Antonio in Texas, and Miami, Orlando and Tampa in Florida.

items.headline: Service impact: Increased Connectivity issues in US-EAST-1
items.summary: We continue to investigate Connectivity issues in the US-EAST-1 Region. IAM Identity center sign-in requests and AWS SignUps are impacted at this time. We can confirm errors when attempted to authenticate when using identity center or when using services that rely on IAM Identity center. For Kiro users, logins from social sign in methods are not impacted at this time. There are no workarounds for impacted customers.
lines: AWS is investigating connectivity issues in the US-EAST-1 Region that affect IAM Identity Center sign-in requests and AWS sign-ups.
Users see authentication errors when signing in through IAM Identity Center or services that rely on it. Logins for Kiro users using social sign-in methods are not affected at this time.
IT teams using IAM Identity Center for access in US-EAST-1 may be unable to sign in, and AWS states there are no workarounds for affected customers.

items.headline: Sources: Apple plans to unveil smart glasses at WWDC and ship them by the end of 2027, focusing heavily on integration of third-party iPhone apps with Siri AI
items.summary: Also: A look at the race to bring Face ID to the iPhone Duo. … Apple's just-announced Siri AI integrations are the centerpiece …
lines: Reported by Bloomberg: Sources say Apple plans to unveil smart glasses at WWDC and ship them by the end of 2027.
The plan focuses heavily on integrating third-party iPhone apps with Siri AI.
Apple's just-announced Siri AI integrations are described as the centerpiece of the plan.

items.headline: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) confirmed that personal employee data has been leaked online after a threat actor put 6.9GB of information allegedly stolen from the company up for auction. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) confirmed that personal employee data has been leaked online.
A threat actor put 6.9GB of information, allegedly stolen from the company, up for auction.
The breach is linked to a cloud provider, which may matter to IT teams reviewing third-party data handling and access controls.
